theory.intro: The rays meeting at a single point divide a full turn into angles that together add to $360^{\circ}$. These are angles **at a point**.
facts: Angles **at a point** (around one vertex) add to $360^{\circ}$.
If all but one angle is known, subtract the total of the known angles from $360^{\circ}$.
steps: Check the angles all meet at one point and fill a full turn.
Subtract from $360^{\circ}$ to find the unknown.

A learner subtracts only $118^{\circ}$ from $360^{\circ}$. Explain and correct the error.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.9]\coordinate (O) at (0,0);\draw (O)--(0:2.3);\draw (O)--(118:2.3);\draw (O)--(205:2.3);\node at (0.35,0.8) {$118^{\circ}$};\node at (-0.8,0.15) {$87^{\circ}$};\node at (0.3,-0.8) {$x$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
development.solution_text:
$118^{\circ}+87^{\circ}+x=360^{\circ}$
$x=360^{\circ}-205^{\circ}$
$=155^{\circ}$
Both known angles must be included before subtracting.

mastery.question_text: Five angles around a point are $48^{\circ}$, $67^{\circ}$, $82^{\circ}$, $x$ and $54^{\circ}$. Find $x$.
Three angles around a point are $35^{\circ}$, an angle $20^{\circ}$ larger than $100^{\circ}$, and $y$. Find $y$.
Four angles at a point include a right angle, $125^{\circ}$, $68^{\circ}$ and $q$. Find $q$.
